category_title: Verbal elementary students with ASD experiencing transition-related outbursts and academic refusal
scenario_title: Academic refusal and emotional outbursts during school transitions
minimal_context: Gabriel is arriving at his general education classroom in the morning and is asked to begin his modified reading assignment.

dialogue.speaker: tutor
dialogue.message: Gabriel, you just arrived at school. Please sit at your desk and start your modified reading assignment.

dialogue.speaker: student
dialogue.message: I don't want to do the reading assignment. I am not doing any school work today.

dialogue.speaker: tutor
dialogue.message: You need to finish your work, Gabriel. Let's get started on the first page.

dialogue.speaker: student
dialogue.message: No! I was at my mom's house this morning, but now I have to go to my dad's house after school. Everything is changing and I don't like it!

dialogue.speaker: tutor
dialogue.message: We can talk about that later. Right now, you need to look at your paper and read.

dialogue.speaker: student
dialogue.message: (Pushes the assignment off the desk and starts crying loudly) I am not doing it! I don't know where I am sleeping tonight! I want my old routine back!

dialogue_combined:
TUTOR: Gabriel, you just arrived at school. Please sit at your desk and start your modified reading assignment.

STUDENT: I don't want to do the reading assignment. I am not doing any school work today.

TUTOR: You need to finish your work, Gabriel. Let's get started on the first page.

STUDENT: No! I was at my mom's house this morning, but now I have to go to my dad's house after school. Everything is changing and I don't like it!

TUTOR: We can talk about that later. Right now, you need to look at your paper and read.

STUDENT: (Pushes the assignment off the desk and starts crying loudly) I am not doing it! I don't know where I am sleeping tonight! I want my old routine back!

task.content: participate in many school assignments and modified assignments

context.environment: general education classroom with typically developing peers, and individual weekly counseling sessions
context.materials: modified assignments, Microsoft Word, photographs, digital pictures provided by Gabriel’s mother, calendar
context.social_setting: participated in the general education classroom with support, and individual counseling with the school counselor
context.time_context: middle of his third-grade year, when arriving to and departing from school

challenging_behavior_trigger.condition: arriving to and departing from school and disrupted family routines due to parents divorcing and living in separate homes
challenging_behavior_trigger.observable_behavior: emotional outbursts when arriving to and departing from school and began refusing to participate in many school assignments
challenging_behavior_trigger.internal_state: emotionally challenging, sensitive to disrupted family routines, due to the rigidity often associated with the disorder

behavior_patterns.condition: resided in both parents’ residences with joint custody
behavior_patterns.observable_behavior: increasingly frequent outbursts at home and academic refusal
behavior_patterns.internal_state: needing to cope with the recent family changes that were impacting his school engagement
